deep.reconstruction:
There are no derivations or formulas on this page beyond the symbol F(α,β,γ,x). Folio 26r is a heavily reworked prose draft of the introduction to Riemann's 1857 memoir 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 7). It is very likely related to his own announcement (Anzeige) in the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen, 1857. The title is written at the top. The surviving argument runs as follows.
(1) The memoir treats a class of functions that render services in solving many problems of mathematical physics and astronomy.
(2) Series built from these functions play, for harder problems, the same role that series in cosines and sines of multiples of a variable (Fourier series) play in simpler cases.
(3) A struck-out sentence says they contain the spherical harmonics (Kugelfunctionen), so important for the physics of the Earth, as special cases.
(4) Euler had occupied himself with these functions repeatedly out of theoretical interest. Their applications, especially astronomical ones, led Gauss to investigate them. Gauss published part of this work in the Commentationes, in the memoir submitted in 1812, where he denotes the series by F(α,β,γ,x).
(5) A definition of the 'hypergeometric series' is attempted several times. It is a series in which the quotient of the (n+1)-th term by the n-th is a rational function of the index (Stellenzeiger).
   - In modern notation: t_{n+1}/t_n = (α+n)(β+n) x / ((n+1)(γ+n)).
   - The previous page contrasts this with the simpler series whose term ratio is a polynomial of first degree in the index.
(6) The unpublished part of Gauss's investigations was found in his Nachlass. Gauss's work had been supplemented by Kummer's papers in vol. 15 of Crelle's Journal (1836; the dates 1835/1836 appear in the image).
(7) Kummer's papers concern transformations of the series into another one in which the variable x is replaced by an algebraic function of x, i.e. Kummer's quadratic and higher transformations. A special case of these transformations had already been recognised earlier.
(8) This continues on the next page: Euler's relation (Euler transformation), Pfaff, Jacobi, the difficulty of the cubic transformation, and Riemann's claim that his method yields all earlier results 'almost without calculation'.
What follows is my supplement, not on the page. The objects referred to are:
   - Gauss's series F(α,β,γ,x) = Σ (α)_n (β)_n / ((γ)_n n!) x^n.
   - Kummer's transformations, e.g. F(a,b,2b,4z/(1+z)^2) = (1+z)^{2a} F(a, a-b+1/2, b+1/2, z^2).
errors: No mathematical errors. The page contains only historical and expository prose.
The historical attributions match the published introduction: Gauss's Commentationes memoir of 1812 and Kummer in Crelle vol. 15 (1836).

results.what: Expository and historical introduction to the memoir on Gauss's hypergeometric series: motivation from mathematical physics, analogy with Fourier series, the Euler–Gauss–Kummer history, and a definition via the rational term ratio.
results.modern_name: Hypergeometric series ₂F₁ (definition by rational term ratio); Kummer's transformations
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (18th c.), Gauss (1812), Kummer (1836); the memoir itself is Riemann 1857

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known introduction to Riemann's published 1857 hypergeometric memoir. It contains no new mathematics, only historical framing that matches the printed text.

transcription_corrections: The dates read in the image as '1836' (struck/inserted) and '1835' (near the margin) refer to Kummer's Crelle vol. 15 papers; the line reads roughly '... durch die im 15 Bande des Journals von Crelle enthaltenen Arbeiten Kummers ergänzt worden'.
Near the bottom the reading is roughly 'Einen speciellen Fall dieser ... Umformungen ... Gauss ... erkannt'.

In the definition of the series, the reading is closer to 'Reihe, in welcher der Quotient des n+1ten Gliedes in das nte ... eine gebrochene Function ... des Stellenzeigers ist'. This is consistent with the rational (not linear) term ratio.
